notes: Triadica sebifera (L.) Small working accepted name; Sapium sebiferum and Croton sebiferum are documented historical names.

morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Distinctive rhombic/ovate long-petioled leaves, then dangling flower spikes and 3-lobed capsules opening to three white wax-coated popcorn-like seeds.

confusers.separator: Confirm Triadica flower spike and popcorn-like 3-seeded capsule.

taxonomy.notes: POWO/WCVP and Flora of North America accept Triadica sebifera.

evidence: POWO explicitly treats Texas as introduced; native range is eastern/central/southern Asia.
Texas A&M Forest Service identifies Chinese tallow as an invasive introduced tree in Central Texas.
US Forest Service FEIS documents introduction and naturalization across the southeastern United States including Texas.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Naturalized/local observations do not qualify as target-zone native evidence.

diagnostics: alternate simple ovate/broadly elliptic to rhomboid leaves with long petioles
two discoid glands near petiole/leaf-base region are useful close-up characters
terminal inflorescences up to about 20 cm
capsule opens to expose three conspicuous white wax-coated popcorn-like seeds

lookalikes.separator: Redbud has different leaf venation/base and lacks Triadica's terminal Euphorbiaceae inflorescences and popcorn-like 3-seeded capsule.
Confirm Triadica petiolar glands, milky sap, inflorescence and 3-lobed capsule/white seeds.

photos.assessment: Existing NPSOT/Texas A&M/USGS/iNaturalist leads can support an invasive-comparison lesson. Best diagnostic set should show leaf shape plus basal/petiolar glands, flower spike, green 3-lobed capsule, and open capsule with white wax-coated seeds.
priority_roles: open capsule with three white seeds

missing_pieces: No native-range evidence can cure the project-native failure because Texas occurrence is introduced/naturalized.
